## Findings
- claim-1: For \(i=j=p=2,c=6\), the accepted \(c=6\) Pieri/Smith output has quotient ranks \(1,1,2,1,1\) in degrees \(4,5,6,7,8\), respectively, and rank \(0\) in degrees \(9,\ldots,32\), with no torsion. Hence \[ Q=J/\Lambda_+J\cong\mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6. \] [artifact 162283c7d25bcc9b6cf77717e180ce1c85e4bdcbe2d0dbabc186aab75e18d126]
- claim-2: With \(r=8,n-r=4,i=j=2\), one has \(a=\min(4-2,8-2)=2\), \(b=2\); the two source families generate \(J\), and each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}=6\) elements. [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: The two generating families specialize to \[ \mathcal F_{\rm top}=\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\}, \qquad \mathcal F_{\rm bot}=\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}. \] Since either six-element family generates \(J\), it induces a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\cong\mathbb Z^6\). By the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion, its images are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q\); therefore no proper subfamily generates \(J\).
- claim-4: The requested new \(i=j=p=2,c=6\) minimality corollary is established: both \(\mathcal F_{\rm top}\) and \(\mathcal F_{\rm bot}\) are minimal generating sets of \(J\).
## Strategy
From the accepted \(c=6\) output, quotient ranks are \(1,1,2,1,1\) in degrees \(4,\dots,8\), and \(0\) thereafter, with no torsion. Thus
\[
Q\cong \mathbb Z^{1+1+2+1+1}=\mathbb Z^6.
\]
For \(r=8,q=4,i=j=2\), \(a=b=2\); each source generating family has six elements:
\[
\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\},\qquad
\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}.
\]
Each generates \(J\), hence maps surjectively \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow Q\). The indexed-family Nakayama criterion makes each map an isomorphism, so no proper subfamily generates \(J\). The requested \(i=j=p=2,c=6\) minimality corollary is established relative to the accepted inputs.
